title: Marketing Coordinator Salary: Hourly Rates, Casual Loading and Super
description: Understand the marketing coordinator salary range, how to convert it to an hourly rate, and what casual loading and super mean for your pay.
salarySummary: A marketing coordinator salary typically ranges from $65,000 to $80,000 per year, which equates to $32.90 to $40.50 per hour based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my marketing coordinator salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. If you are a casual marketing coordinator, your hourly rate would be the base rate multiplied by 1.25. For example, if the base rate is $35.00 per hour, the casual rate would be $43.75 per hour. This loading is separate from superannuation, which is paid on top of the total ordinary earnings.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a marketing coordinator salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at the current super guarantee rate of 12%. For a marketing coordinator earning $70,000 per year, the super contribution would be $8,400 per year, bringing the total cost to the employer to $78,400. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional payment into a super fund. The maximum earnings subject to super is $270,830 per year.

faqs.q: How do I convert a marketing coordinator salary to an hourly rate?
faqs.a: To convert an annual salary to an hourly rate, divide the annual salary by 52 weeks, then divide by the number of hours worked per week. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate = annual salary ÷ 52 ÷ 38. For example, a $70,000 salary gives $70,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = $35.43 per hour. If you are casual, add 25% casual loading to this base rate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Marketing Coordinator Salary

If you're looking at a marketing coordinator salary, you're likely seeing figures between $65,000 and $80,000 per year, according to the Ampersand Salary Guide 2025. However, that guide is a recruiter survey, not an official award or minimum wage. For the most authoritative rates, always check the Fair Work Commission or the Fair Work Ombudsman. The national minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A marketing coordinator salary is usually above that, but the exact figure depends on your award, experience, and location.

### Converting a Marketing Coordinator Salary to an Hourly Rate

To work out your hourly rate from an annual salary, use the formula: hourly rate = annual salary ÷ 52 weeks ÷ hours per week. We assume a standard 38-hour full-time week. For example:

- $65,000 per year → $65,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = $32.90 per hour
- $75,000 per year → $75,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = $37.95 per hour
- $80,000 per year → $80,000 ÷ 52 ÷ 38 = $40.50 per hour

If you work fewer hours, your hourly rate will be higher, but the 38-hour week is the standard used by the Fair Work Commission.

### Casual Loading and Your Marketing Coordinator Salary

If you work as a casual marketing coordinator, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is set by the Fair Work Act and applies to award/agreement-free employees. For example, if your base rate is $35.00 per hour, the casual rate becomes $43.75 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this in more detail. Remember: never type a rate that already includes casual loading into the timesheet; use the base rate and check the casual loading box.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a marketing coordinator earning $70,000 per year, that's an extra $8,400 per year into your super fund. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost for the employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is your weekly rate multiplied by two. For a $70,000 salary, weekly pay is $1,346.15 (70,000 ÷ 52), so fortnightly is $2,692.30. The [the timesheet](/) can help you calculate take-home pay after tax and Medicare.

### Tax on Your Marketing Coordinator Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Tax Office tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). A marketing coordinator earning $75,000 would pay approximately $13,167 in tax and $1,500 in Medicare levy, leaving a take-home pay of about $60,333 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed estimate.

### Award Rates vs Market Salary

The marketing coordinator role may be covered by the Professional Employees Award or the Clerks Award, depending on duties. Award rates are minimums; your actual marketing coordinator salary may be higher. Check the Fair Work Commission's [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) for the latest award rates. The national minimum wage is the floor, but most marketing coordinators earn above it.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It calculates annual, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly figures, plus estimated tax and super. For a marketing coordinator salary, enter your hourly rate (e.g., $35.00) and select 38 hours per week. The tool will show you the full picture.

### Summary

A marketing coordinator salary of $65,000 to $80,000 per year translates to $32.90 to $40.50 per hour for a 38-hour week. If you are casual, add 25% loading. Super is 12% on top. Always verify your rate against the relevant award or the national minimum wage. For more conversions, see the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page.
